### Q2 — CORE number variant twin
**LO:** LO 14-2  
**Concept:** number_variant_twin — same TS FV-NI path with all new amounts  
**Scenario:**  
On **January 1 of Year 1**, **Harborpeak Capital LLC** purchased for **par $40,000** of **Redwood Corp. 6%** bonds that mature on December 31 of Year 8. Cash interest is paid **annually** each December 31. Harborpeak classifies the bonds as **trading securities (TS)** under **FV-NI**. Year-end is December 31. Beginning FVA—TS is zero. No other TS activity except as stated.

| Date | Fair value / activity |
|---|---|
| Dec 31, Year 1 | Fair value **$38,500** |
| Dec 31, Year 2 | Still held; fair value **$41,200** |
| Jan 1, Year 3 | Sold entire holding for **$41,000** |

**Required:**  
(a) Purchase entry on January 1 of Year 1.  
(b) Cash interest entry on December 31 of Year 1.  
(c) Fair value adjustment on December 31 of Year 1 (include FVA schedule).  
(d) Year 1 BS / IS presentation for this investment.  
(e) December 31, Year 2 FVA rollforward schedule and adjusting entry.  
(f) January 1, Year 3 sale: (i) sale-date FV-NI adjust; (ii) sale eliminating FVA.  
(g) Holding-period unrealized G/L schedule proving cumulative NI = proceeds − cost.

### Q1 — CORE — Equity method with basis difference: initial recognition, period-end adjusting JEs, and investment schedule (emphasis)
**LO:** LO 14-5  
**Concept:** Period-end equity-method adjusting entries (share of NI, excess depreciation on basis difference, dividends as return of investment) and investment account rollforward  
**Scenario:**  
**Cascade Harbor Holdings** (calendar-year) acquires a long-term equity interest in **Meridian Forge Co.** on **January 1, Year 1**. Cascade can exercise **significant influence** and applies the **equity method**.

| Fact | Amount / term |
|---|---|
| Cash purchase price (Jan 1, Year 1) | **$240,000** |
| Ownership interest | **30%** of Meridian’s voting common stock |
| Meridian stockholders’ equity (book value of net assets) at acquisition | **$700,000** |
| Fair value of Meridian’s net assets exceeds book value solely due to undervalued **equipment** | Equipment undervalued by **$40,000** total on Meridian’s books |
| Remaining useful life of the undervalued equipment | **8 years**, straight-line, no residual |
| Remainder of Cascade’s cost over share of fair value of net assets | Attributable to **goodwill** (not amortized) |
| Meridian net income for Year 1 | **$80,000** |
| Meridian cash dividends declared and paid Dec 31, Year 1 | **$20,000** |
| Fair value of Cascade’s 30% interest at Dec 31, Year 1 | **$255,000** |

**Required:**  
a. Record the **January 1, Year 1 initial recognition** journal entry. Briefly support why the equity method applies.  
b. Allocate the **$240,000** cost among share of book value, depreciable basis difference, and goodwill.  
c. Record all **December 31, Year 1 period-end adjusting** journal entries under the equity method (share of NI, excess depreciation, dividends). State whether any fair-value adjustment is recorded.  
d. Prepare the **subsequent measurement (Investment) schedule** for Year 1 and compute the Dec 31 carrying amount.  
e. Compute **net equity-method income** recognized in Year 1 (investment income after excess depreciation).

### Q3 — CORE — Multi-security FVA schedule after mid-year disposal (period-end only)

**LO:** LO 14-7  
**Concept:** subsequent_measurement_schedule; disposal_maturity_or_settlement_JE; period_end_adjusting_JE; classification_presentation_or_disclosure  
**Scenario:**  
Lakeview Holdings measures its **trading** debt securities at FV-NI and adjusts the **Fair Value Adjustment—TS** account **only at December 31** each year (not on sale dates).  

At January 1 of Year 2, the Fair Value Adjustment—TS account has a **credit balance of $3,200**.

During Year 2:  
- June 12: Sold the entire Crest 4.5% bond position (amortized cost **$35,000**) for cash **$33,800**.  
- No other purchases or sales of TS.

Securities still held at December 31 of Year 2:

| Security | Amortized Cost | Fair Value 12/31/Y2 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Dune 5% bonds | $25,000 | $24,100 |
| Pier 4% bonds | 60,000 | 61,500 |
| **Total remaining** | **$85,000** | **$85,600** |

**Required:**  
a. Record the June 12 sale of Crest under the period-end-only method.  
b. Prepare the year-end subsequent measurement / FVA schedule for the remaining portfolio.  
c. Record the December 31 of Year 2 FVA adjusting entry.  
d. Show how Investment in trading securities is reported on the December 31, Year 2 balance sheet.  
e. Compute the Year 2 income statement effect from (i) the Crest sale and (ii) the period-end FVA adjustment (ignore interest).

### Q4 — CORE — HTM → AFS transfer and subsequent AFS period-end adjustment
**LO:** LO 14-10  
**Concept:** HTM → AFS transfer at fair value through OCI (no NI); subsequent AFS FVA period-end JE  
**Scenario:**  
Lakeshore Mutual Fund holds the following **HTM** portfolio at **December 31, Year 3**. All bonds were purchased at **par**.

| Security | Amortized cost | Fair value (Dec 31, Y3) | Unrealized gain (loss) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Quill Corp. bonds | $90,000 | $96,300 | $6,300 |
| Dune Partners bonds | 60,000 | 55,800 | (4,200) |
| **Total** | **$150,000** | **$152,100** | **$2,100** |

On **January 1, Year 4**, because of a significant deterioration in the issuers’ credit standings, Lakeshore changes intent and **transfers both securities from HTM to AFS**. Fair values on the transfer date equal the December 31, Year 3 amounts above.

At **December 31, Year 4**, fair values are: Quill **$94,000**; Dune **$57,000**. Lakeshore adjusts AFS securities to fair value at year-end through OCI.

**Required:**  
a. Record the **January 1, Year 4** transfer entries (reclassify HTM → AFS and recognize transfer-date FV through OCI).  
b. State the transfer-date effect on NI and OCI.  
c. Record the **December 31, Year 4** AFS fair-value adjusting entry.  
d. Briefly state what footnote disclosure should accompany a transfer of this type.

### Q1 — CORE — Between-interest TS purchase, period-end FVA (emphasis), sale vs AC, year-end FVA cleanup

**LO:** LO 14-7  
**Concept:** Initial recognition of trading debt securities; cash interest; **period-end-only** FV-NI adjusting JE (emphasis); disposal with realized G/L vs amortized cost; subsequent period-end FVA elimination  
**Scenario:**  
**Larkspur Trading Partners** (calendar year) buys debt for short-term price appreciation and classifies it as **trading securities (TS)** measured at **FV-NI**. Per company policy (Appendix 14A / LO 14-7), Larkspur records **Fair Value Adjustment (FVA)** entries **only at each December 31 period-end**—never on sale dates.

**Facts:**
1. On **November 1, Year 1**, Larkspur purchases **at par** **$60,000** face of **Cascade Biologics** **9%** bonds (bonds dated **July 1, Year 1**; mature **June 30, Year 7**). Cash interest is paid **semiannually on June 30 and December 31**. No brokerage fees.
2. Fair value of the Cascade bonds on **December 31, Year 1** is **$57,000**.
3. On **March 15, Year 2**, Larkspur sells the entire holding for **$57,600** cash (clean price; ignore any March accrued-interest complexity beyond the facts given).
4. After the sale, Larkspur holds **no other TS**. It next adjusts FVA only on **December 31, Year 2**.

**Required:**  
a. Prepare the **November 1, Year 1 initial recognition JE** (include accrued interest paid to seller).  
b. Prepare the **December 31, Year 1** cash interest receipt JE.  
c. Prepare a **period-end FVA worksheet** and the **December 31, Year 1 period-end adjusting JE** (emphasis).  
d. Show **Year 1 balance-sheet carrying amount** and **income-statement** effects (interest + unrealized G/L).  
e. Prepare the **March 15, Year 2 disposal JE** under LO 14-7 (realized G/L vs amortized cost; **do not** adjust FVA at sale).  
f. Prepare the **December 31, Year 2 period-end adjusting JE** that eliminates leftover FVA, and a **holding-period G/L reconciliation** schedule.

### Q2 — CORE number variant — Copper Ridge Utilities: different face, yield, retirement fraction, call price
**LO:** LO 16-7  
**Concept:** Number-variant twin — effective-interest life cycle with 50% early extinguishment at 103 after period-end update  
**Scenario:**  
On January 1, Year 1, Copper Ridge Utilities issued **$400,000** face of **4-year, 6%** bonds. Cash interest is payable annually each December 31. Bonds were priced to yield **8%** and sold for **$373,503** (discount **$26,497**). Effective interest method; year-end December 31.

On **December 31, Year 2**, after the period-end interest entry and cash interest payment, Copper Ridge retires **50%** of the bonds in the open market at **103**. The remaining 50% is held through maturity.

**Required:**  
a. Record issuance on January 1, Year 1.  
b. Prepare the full effective-interest amortization schedule (Years 1–4).  
c. Record December 31, Year 2 period-end interest, then the 50% extinguishment (show gain/loss computation).  
d. Prepare the remaining-half interest entries conceptually for Year 3 and Year 4 and the maturity entry on December 31, Year 4.

### Q2 — CORE number variant — Discount bond twin (issue, full schedule, interest, maturity, presentation)
**LO:** LO 16-2  
**Concept:** Number-variant twin: recompute issue price when market > stated; effective-interest subsequent measurement schedule; interest JEs; maturity settlement; net presentation  
**Scenario:**  
**Cascade Peak Logistics Inc.** issues **$250,000** face of **6%** bonds on **January 1, Year 1**. Bonds mature **December 31, Year 4** (4 years), pay interest **semiannually** on June 30 and December 31, and were priced to yield a **market rate of 8%**. Cascade uses the **effective interest method** (round to nearest dollar; plug residual amort in the final period).

**Required:**  
a. Compute the **issue price** and prepare the **initial recognition JE**.  
b. Prepare the **full effective-interest amortization schedule** (8 periods).  
c. Prepare the **June 30, Year 1** and **December 31, Year 1** interest + amortization JEs.  
d. Report **bonds payable, net** and **Year 1 interest expense** at December 31, Year 1.  
e. Prepare the **maturity** entries on December 31, Year 4 (final interest + principal repayment; no prior Interest Payable).

### Q1 — CORE — Detachable warrants (proportional), premium amort schedule, period-end interest, exercise, expiration, maturity
**LO:** LO 16-11  
**Concept:** Proportional allocation of detachable bond-with-warrants proceeds; subsequent straight-line premium amortization schedule; period-end interest adjusting JE; warrant exercise and expiration; bond maturity  
**Scenario:**  
**Riverbend Packaging Co.** (calendar-year company) issues bonds with **detachable** stock purchase warrants on **January 1, Year 1**.

| Fact | Amount / term |
|---|---|
| Face amount | **$600,000** of 7%, 5-year nonconvertible bonds |
| Interest | Payable **annually each December 31** |
| Bond unit | Each **$1,000** bond carries **10** detachable warrants |
| Total warrants | \(600 \times 10 = \mathbf{6{,}000}\) warrants |
| Exercise terms | Each warrant: one share of **$5** par common for **$22** cash |
| Package issue price | **105** (bonds + warrants) → cash proceeds **$630,000** |
| Fair value shortly after issuance | Bonds **without** warrants quoted at **102**; warrants trade at **$3** each |
| Debt amortization | **Straight-line** amortization of premium over **5 years** |

On **March 1, Year 3**, holders exercise **4,500** warrants. The remaining **1,500** warrants expire unexercised on **January 15, Year 4**. Bonds are held to maturity and settled on **December 31, Year 5** (after the Year-5 interest payment).

**Required:**  
a. Allocate the **$630,000** package proceeds to bonds and warrants using the **proportional method**. Compute the initial bond carrying amount and premium.  
b. Record the **January 1, Year 1** initial recognition journal entry.  
c. Prepare a complete **subsequent measurement amortization schedule** for Years 1–5 (beginning carrying amount, cash interest, premium amortization, interest expense, ending carrying amount).  
d. Record the **December 31, Year 1** period-end interest adjusting journal entry.  
e. Record the **March 1, Year 3** exercise of 4,500 warrants.  
f. Record the **January 15, Year 4** expiration of the remaining 1,500 warrants.  
g. Record the **December 31, Year 5** maturity (settlement) entry for the bonds (interest already recorded separately).  
h. In one or two sentences, explain why Paid-In Capital—Stock Warrants is **not** amortized over the bond term.

### Q1 — CORE — Interest-bearing note issued for cash at a discount (full lifecycle)
**LO:** LO 16-6  
**Concept:** Initial recognition JE + effective-interest schedule + period-end interest JE + maturity settlement  
**Scenario:** On January 1, Year 1, **Redwood Metalworks Inc.** borrows cash by issuing a **3-year, $80,000** note payable to Northshore Bank. The note pays **5%** cash interest annually each December 31. The market rate for notes of similar risk is **9%**. Redwood’s fiscal year ends December 31. Redwood uses the **effective interest method**.

**Required:**  
(a) Compute the cash proceeds (issue price) of the note on January 1, Year 1. Round the present value to the nearest cent.  
(b) Record the **initial recognition** journal entry on January 1, Year 1.  
(c) Prepare the complete **effective-interest amortization schedule** over the 3-year term (show cash interest, interest expense, discount amortization, and carrying amount). Plug any final-period rounding difference so the carrying amount equals face at maturity.  
(d) Record the **December 31, Year 1** interest entry (period-end).  
(e) Record the **December 31, Year 3** interest entry and the **maturity settlement** entry (principal only may be shown separately from interest).

### Q3 — CORE alternate angle — Straight-line discount schedule, interest JEs, maturity
**LO:** LO 16-4  
**Concept:** Straight-line interest method for discount amortization (constant amort. per period); interest JE pattern; maturity when discount fully amortized; contrast with effective interest  
**Scenario:**  
**Cascade Brewing Co.** issues **$100,000** face of **8%** annual interest bonds on **January 1, Year 1**. Interest is paid **annually** each **December 31**. The bonds mature **December 31, Year 3**. Bonds are sold for **$95,026** (market yield **10%** at issuance). Cascade amortizes the discount using the **straight-line interest method** (assume results are not materially different from effective interest for this illustration).

- Initial discount = $100,000 − $95,026 = **$4,974**
- Annual cash interest = 8% × $100,000 = **$8,000**
- Straight-line discount amortization per year = $4,974 ÷ 3 = **$1,658**
- Annual interest expense = $8,000 + $1,658 = **$9,658**

**Required:**  
a. January 1, Year 1 issuance JE.  
b. Straight-line amortization schedule for Years 1–3.  
c. December 31, Year 1 and Year 2 interest/amortization JEs.  
d. December 31, Year 3 final interest JE and maturity settlement JE.  
e. **Classification / method note:** Under GAAP (ASC 835-30), when is straight-line acceptable relative to the effective interest method? Where is the unamortized discount reported?

### Q3 — CORE alternate angle — DDB schedule (residual floor) + SYD Year 1 + UOP Year 1 + disposal
**LO:** LO 12-1  
**Concept:** Double-declining-balance subsequent measurement schedule with residual-value floor (final-year plug); SYD and units-of-production Year 1 expense; period-end dep JE; disposal after three years under DDB  
**Scenario:**  
**Riverton Machine Co.** buys production equipment on **January 1, Year 1** for **$50,000 cash**. Residual value **$5,000**; useful life **5 years**; estimated total productive output **10,000 units**.

Actual production Year 1: **1,800 units**.

Riverton wants to understand all four LO 12-1 methods, then elects **double-declining-balance (DDB)** for books.

On **December 31, Year 3**, after recording Year 3 DDB depreciation, Riverton **sells** the equipment for **$12,000 cash**.

**Required:**  
a. Compute Year 1 depreciation under **straight-line**, **sum-of-the-years’-digits**, **double-declining-balance**, and **units-of-production**. Record the **Year 1 period-end adjusting JE** assuming DDB is used.  
b. Prepare the full **DDB subsequent measurement schedule** for Years 1–5. Show the residual-value floor / plug in the final year.  
c. Record the **initial recognition JE** and the **December 31, Year 3 disposal settlement JE** under DDB (after Year 3 depreciation). State gain or loss.  
d. In one sentence, explain why DDB does **not** subtract residual value when applying the rate, yet still ends at residual.

### Q3 — CORE alternate angle — multi-asset recoverability screen + year-end impairment + post-write-down schedule
**LO:** LO 12-7  
**Concept:** Period-end multi-asset recoverability (pass vs fail); combined impairment JE only for failed assets; **subsequent measurement schedule** with nonzero residual on the written-down asset  
**Scenario:**  
At **December 31, Year 3**, **Redwood Circuits LLC** identifies impairment indicators for three plant assets **currently used in operations**. Management provides:

| Asset | Cost | Accumulated depreciation | Recoverable cost (undiscounted) | Fair value |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| A — Precision press | $400,000 | $100,000 | $350,000 | $280,000 |
| B — Curing oven | $700,000 | $200,000 | $420,000 | $310,000 |
| C — Assembly conveyor | $900,000 | $150,000 | $750,000 | $600,000 |

After any required write-down, Asset B will be used **5 more years** with a revised residual of **$10,000** (straight-line). Assets A and C continue under their pre-existing policies (no change requested here).

**Required:**  
a. For each asset, compute carrying amount, apply the **recoverability test**, and state any **impairment loss**. Assume indicators are present for all three.  
b. Record a **single December 31, Year 3** journal entry for all impairment losses required (if any).  
c. For **Asset B only**, prepare the **subsequent measurement schedule** of depreciation for the five years after the write-down (Years 4–8). Record the December 31, Year 4 depreciation entry for Asset B.  
d. Briefly explain why an asset with fair value **below** carrying amount might still have **no** impairment loss.

### Q2 — CORE number variant — Life extended, residual cut, disposal with loss
**LO:** LO 12-4  
**Concept:** Number-variant twin: initial PPE recognition; SL schedule; prospective change in useful life and residual; updated period-end dep; disposal with loss  
**Scenario:**  
**Coastal Glassworks Inc.** (calendar year) places a tempering furnace into service on **January 1, Year 1**.

| **January 1, Year 5** change in estimate | Total useful life revised to **12 years**; residual revised to **$12,000** |

b. Original annual depreciation; depreciation schedule for Years 1–4.  
c. Carrying amount at January 1, Year 5; updated annual depreciation; Year 5 period-end JE.  
d. Schedule Years 5–12 (spot-check that residual is reached at end of Year 12).  
e. Disposal JE on December 31, Year 6.  
f. One-sentence classification: is this a change in principle, error correction, or estimate?

### Q1 — CORE — Multi-security ranking schedule, sequential diluted EPS, initial recognition & period-end JEs (emphasis: subsequent measurement schedule)
**LO:** LO 20-9  
**Concept:** Initial recognition of convertible securities; subsequent measurement ranking and sequential diluted EPS schedules; period-end preferred dividend and bond interest JEs; dual face presentation of basic and diluted EPS  
**Scenario:**  
**Meridian Cascade Holdings Inc.** is a calendar-year public company with a **complex capital structure**. For the year ended December 31, Year 1:

| Item | Amount |
|---|---:|
| Net income | $380,000 |
| Weighted-average common shares outstanding (entire year) | 200,000 |
| Income tax rate | 25% |

There are **no** discontinued operations. On **January 1, Year 1**, Meridian issued the following securities (all outstanding the entire year; none exercised or converted during Year 1). Common stock has a **$1 par** value.

1. **Employee stock options:** 10,000 options to purchase one common share each at an exercise price of **$20**. Average market price of common stock during Year 1: **$40**.
2. **5% cumulative convertible preferred stock:** 4,000 shares, **$100 par**, issued at par. Each preferred share is convertible into **3** common shares. Preferred dividends for the full year were declared and paid on December 31.
3. **Series X convertible bonds:** **$500,000** face, **4%** coupon, issued at par on January 1. Each **$1,000** bond is convertible into **25** common shares. Interest was paid in cash for the full year.
4. **Series Y convertible bonds:** **$300,000** face, **10%** coupon, issued at par on January 1. Each **$1,000** bond is convertible into **8** common shares. Interest was paid in cash for the full year.

**Required:**  
a. Prepare the **January 1, Year 1 initial recognition journal entries** for (1) the convertible preferred stock issuance and (2) the Series X convertible bond issuance. Show Dr = Cr.  
b. Compute the **numerator effect**, **denominator effect**, and **earnings per incremental share** for each potentially dilutive security. **Rank** the securities from most dilutive to least dilutive.  
c. Compute **basic EPS** for Year 1.  
d. Prepare the **sequential diluted EPS subsequent measurement schedule** (most dilutive → least dilutive). Identify which securities are dilutive vs antidilutive and state **diluted EPS**.  
e. Prepare the **December 31, Year 1 period-end journal entries** for (1) the annual preferred dividend (cash paid same day) and (2) full-year cash interest on Series X bonds. Show Dr = Cr.  
f. Show the **financial statement presentation** of basic and diluted EPS on the face of the income statement.

### Q2 — CORE number variant — ESPP twin (all numbers changed)
**LO:** LO 20-3  
**Concept:** Number-variant twin: subsequent measurement liability schedule; initial recognition of noncompensatory and compensatory ESPP issuances; period-end withholding; settlement JE; total compensation expense  
**Scenario:**  
**Silverbrook Medical Devices Inc.** (calendar-year) has **$2 par** common stock and two ESPP arrangements.

**Plan N (noncompensatory design):** Substantially all eligible employees may participate equitably; purchase price = **95% of market** on the purchase date; refunds of withholdings allowed if participation is canceled before purchase; enrollment window after price is fixed does not exceed 31 days.

**Plan C (compensatory design):** Only designated high performers may participate; purchase price = **90% of market** on the purchase date.

**Cash purchases on September 30, Year 1** (market price **$48**):  
- Plan N: employees buy **3,000 shares** for cash.  
- Plan C: employees buy **2,000 shares** for cash.

**Payroll-funded Plan N cohort (January 1 – June 30, Year 1 offering):**  
Monthly withholdings **$11,400** for six months credited to Liability—ESPP. On June 30, market price is **$40**; Plan N price = 95% of market. Whole shares only; exact fit. No cancellations.

**Required:**  
a. Classify Plan N and Plan C.  
b. Prepare the **September 30 Plan N** initial recognition JE.  
c. Prepare the **September 30 Plan C** initial recognition JE.  
d. Prepare the **six-month Liability—ESPP accumulation schedule** and compute shares issued at June 30.  
e. Prepare the **representative January 31 period-end withholding JE** and the **June 30 settlement JE** for the payroll cohort.  
f. Compute **total compensation expense** recognized in Year 1 from these ESPP transactions (cash purchases + payroll cohort).

### Q1 — CORE — Share issuance, buyback, preferred dividend, stock dividend: JEs + WAS + basic EPS
**LO:** LO 20-5  
**Concept:** Initial recognition JEs for issuance, treasury buyback, preferred dividend, and large stock dividend; weighted-average shares schedule with retroactive stock-dividend factor; basic EPS and income-statement presentation  
**Scenario:**  
**Northlake Precision Inc.** has a simple capital structure and a calendar year. On **January 1, 2025**, the company has:

| Item | Amount |
|---|---|
| Common stock outstanding | **120,000** shares, **$2** par |
| Cumulative preferred stock outstanding | **8,000** shares, **6%**, **$25** par (outstanding all year) |
| Net income for 2025 | **$378,000** |

Equity activity during 2025:

| Date | Event |
|---|---|
| **April 1** | Issued **30,000** common shares for cash at **$14** per share. |
| **July 1** | Purchased **6,000** common shares for the **treasury** at **$16** per share (shares remain outstanding legally but are not outstanding for EPS). |
| **September 30** | Declared and paid cash dividends equal to the **full annual preferred claim**. |
| **November 1** | Declared and distributed a **20%** common stock dividend. Market price that day is **$18**. Treat the 20% stock dividend as a **large** stock dividend and record at **par**. |

No common cash dividends affect the EPS numerator. Ignore income taxes.

**Required:**  
a. Prepare the **initial recognition journal entries** for April 1 (issuance), July 1 (buyback), September 30 (preferred dividend), and November 1 (stock dividend). Show Dr = Cr for each.  
b. Prepare a **weighted-average common shares schedule** for 2025, applying the **retroactive restatement** factor for the stock dividend to all periods before November 1.  
c. Compute **income available to common stockholders** and **basic EPS** for 2025 (round EPS to the nearest cent).  
d. Show how **basic EPS** is **presented** on the 2025 income statement (simple capital structure).  
e. Briefly explain why the stock dividend is treated differently from the April 1 cash issuance in the denominator.

### Q3 — CORE alternate angle — 100% stock dividend retroactive restatement; issuance; buyback; noncumulative preferred
**LO:** LO 20-5  
**Concept:** Weighted-average shares with **retroactive restatement** for a large stock dividend; mid-year issuance and buyback JEs; large stock dividend capitalization JE; noncumulative preferred dividends (subtract only when declared); basic EPS schedule  
**Scenario:**  
**Lakeshore Fiber Optics Ltd.** is a calendar-year public company. No convertibles, options, or warrants. No noncontrolling interest.

**Beginning of Year 1 (already outstanding):**
- **50,000** shares of **$1 par** common stock
- **5,000** shares of **6%, $100 par noncumulative** preferred stock (outstanding all year)

**Year 1 equity transactions:**
| Date | Event |
|---|---|
| **April 1** | Issues **10,000** shares of $1 par common for **$20** cash per share |
| **July 1** | Purchases **5,000** common shares for the **treasury** at **$22** cash per share (cost method) |
| **October 1** | Distributes a **100% common stock dividend** (one new share for each share then outstanding). Fair value is irrelevant for this large stock dividend; capitalize **par** of shares issued. Market price on October 1 is $24 (given for context only). |
| **December 10** | Declares and immediately pays **$30,000** cash dividends on the **noncumulative** preferred stock (the full stated annual amount). No common cash dividend is declared. |

**Finalized Year 1 net income** (after all income-statement items, including tax) is **$360,000**. (Treat NI as given—no separate income AJs required in this item.)

**Required:**  
a. Prepare the **April 1** common stock **issuance** journal entry.  
b. Prepare the **July 1** treasury stock **purchase** journal entry.  
c. Prepare the **October 1 large stock dividend** journal entry (par capitalization). State shares outstanding immediately before and after the dividend.  
d. Prepare the **December 10** preferred dividend **declaration and payment** (may be combined or shown as two entries).  
e. Prepare the **weighted-average common shares schedule** applying the **retroactive restatement factor** for the 100% stock dividend to all periods **before** October 1.  
f. Prepare the **basic EPS computation schedule**. Explain in one sentence why the noncumulative preferred dividend is subtracted and how stock-dividend treatment differs from the April cash issuance.

### Q3 — CORE alternate angle — Period-end LCM JE focus: ceiling/floor edge cases, COGS vs holding loss, two-year allowance true-up

**LO:** LO 10-2  
**Concept:** **Period-end adjusting JE emphasis** — compute designated market from ceiling/floor/RC edge cases; record Year 1 write-down two ways; Year 2 allowance true-up after full turnover of prior layer; BS/IS presentation  
**Scenario:**  
**Aspen Forge Tools Inc.** measures inventory with **LIFO** and applies **LCM by individual item**. It uses an **Allowance to Reduce Inventory to Market** and adjusts the allowance **only at December 31**. **Concept:** Subsequent measurement schedule for multi-year warranty liability; initial recognition of probable litigation; period-end warranty and contingency accruals; settlement JE; commitment/contingency disclosures; current and quick ratios before/after Year-2 accruals  
**Scenario:**  
**Silverpine Fitness Equipment Co.** (calendar-year) sells fitness machines with assurance-type warranties. Management prepares a multi-year warranty liability rollforward and evaluates litigation contingencies, commitments, and liquidity at December 31, **Year 2**. Statements for Year 2 will be issued March 12, Year 3.

**Warranty facts (assurance-type; multi-year subsequent measurement):**

| Year | Product sales | Estimated warranty cost rate | Actual warranty claims paid in cash during year |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | $4,800,000 | 2.5% of sales | $105,000 |
| 2 | $5,400,000 | 2.5% of sales | $118,000 |
| 3 | $5,700,000 | 2.0% of sales | $122,000 |

Warranty liability, **January 1, Year 1** (beginning balance): **$52,000**.

**Company policy:** During each year, cash claims are debited to **Warranty Expense** as incurred. At each year-end, Silverpine records an adjusting entry so that **ending warranty liability = beginning warranty liability + estimated warranty cost for that year’s sales − claims paid that year**. Total warranty expense for a year equals estimated warranty cost for that year’s sales.

**Litigation (Year 2):** In Year 2 a customer filed suit alleging injury from a defective machine. Outside counsel concludes a loss is **probable**. Estimated range of loss: **$120,000–$250,000**; the **best estimate** within the range is **$160,000**. Nothing has been recorded yet at December 31, Year 2.

**Settlement (Year 3):** On March 5, Year 3 (before Year-2 statements are issued), the suit settles for cash of **$175,000**. Counsel confirms the settlement relates to conditions existing at December 31, Year 2. For the instructional Year-2 initial-recognition and ratio parts below, first record the **$160,000** best-estimate accrual; then address settlement / remeasurement separately.

**Commitments at December 31, Year 2 (not on books):**
- Unused bank letter of credit: **$600,000**
- Noncancelable contract to acquire a production plant expansion for **$1,500,000** (closing expected May Year 3)

**Unadjusted balances at December 31, Year 2** (after recording Year-2 warranty *claims* as Warranty Expense, but **before** the Year-2 warranty true-up and **before** the litigation accrual). Warranty liability on the books is still the **January 1, Year 2** balance.

| Current liabilities | Amount |

**Required:**

Then record the **March 5, Year 3 settlement JE** against the $160,000 Year-2 accrual when cash of $175,000 is paid. Briefly state how Year-2 issued statements would treat the $175,000 settlement if it is a **recognized subsequent event**.
